property_summary: Once airdrop is successfully called, tokenBalance[caller] must never exceed 20 (initial 20) because hasNoBalance prevents second mint; the bug removes this gate so repeated calls increase balance beyond 20.
For any caller, after any sequence of airDrop calls, the caller's tokenBalance must be exactly 0 or exactly 20; the bug allows the same caller to exceed 20.
For any caller, tokenBalance[caller] after a successful airDrop must be exactly 20; the bug allows repeated calls by the same address to increase the balance beyond 20.

After any execution of airDrop, the tokenBalance of any single address must be at most 20 because hasNoBalance prevents a second mint; the bug removes this check, allowing a caller's balance to exceed 20.
For any caller, a successful airDrop must increase tokenBalance by exactly 20, but the mutant's increase of 21 violates this invariant.

For any caller, after a successful airDrop, the tokenBalance of msg.sender must increase by EXACTLY 20; the mutant can allow a caller to execute airDrop even if they already have a non-zero balance, causing tokenBalance to increase repeatedly beyond the intended one-time airdrop, breaking the invariant.

After any sequence of calls, the total supply (sum of all tokenBalances) equals exactly 20 times the number of successful airDrop calls; the mutant allows multiple airDrops per address, breaking this invariant.

After any call to airDrop, no address except the caller can have its tokenBalance changed; the buggy mutant allows zero-balance callers to still succeed, but the invariant holds for the reference because the hasNoBalance modifier ensures the caller starts at 0, and the overflow check is always true for 20, so the only balance change is +20 for the caller.

For any caller and any external Bank, the airDrop function either reverts or increments the caller's tokenBalance by exactly 20; the mutant bypasses the reentrancy guard by allowing an adversarial Bank to re-enter airDrop, causing the caller's tokenBalance to increase by more than 20.

After any number of airDrop calls by any addresses, the sum of all tokenBalance values must remain a multiple of 20; the buggy version breaks this because the permanent lock prevents a second call from adding 20, so the total can remain at 20 instead of increasing to 40.

After any sequence of airDrop calls by distinct addresses, the number of callers with a non-zero tokenBalance must equal the number of distinct successful callers; the bug's permanent lock causes a second call by a different address to revert, leaving only one address with a non-zero balance but two addresses attempted to call.

After any number of calls to airDrop, the sum of all tokenBalance entries modulo 20 is always zero; the buggy permanent lock allows only the first call to succeed, leaving a sum of 20 which breaks the invariant when a second distinct caller attempts the airdrop.

After any single successful airdrop, the _locked flag must be false (the modifier is non-reentrant, not permanent); the bug leaves _locked true permanently, so a second caller will revert instead of receiving tokens.

For every caller with no prior balance, a successful airDrop increases total supply by exactly 20 and leaves the contract unlocked; the permanent lock prevents any second caller from ever receiving tokens, so total supply remains 20 after two distinct zero‑balance callers attempt the drop.

For any caller satisfying the original airdrop preconditions, a successful airDrop increases tokenBalance[caller] by 20 in the reference, while the mutant's supportsToken modifier always reverts (or prevents balance change) when Bank(msg.sender) returns the original token name, leaving tokenBalance[caller] unchanged.

For any caller that is a Bank contract returning the 'Nu Token' name, the reference's airDrop always increases the caller's tokenBalance by 20; the mutant reverts because its supportsToken modifier requires a different token name.

In the original contract, an airdrop can succeed for any caller whose Bank returns the correct token name, but with the changed string, the modifier never matches, so tokenBalance will remain 0 for all addresses after the call.

For any caller that is a Bank contract returning the 'Nu Token' name, a successful airDrop increases the caller's tokenBalance by 20; the mutant reverts because its supportsToken modifier requires a different token name.

For any caller that is a Bank contract deployed by the fuzzer returning the original token name, the reference airDrop always succeeds and increases the caller's tokenBalance by 20, while the mutant reverts.
